questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's Navratnas:
Statement 1: Tansen, originally named Ramtanu Pandey, was one of the Navratnas in the court of Akbar.
Statement 2: Amir Khusro was also one of the Navratnas of Akbar.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Tansen, a legendary musician known as 'Sangeet Samrat', was indeed one of Akbar's Navratnas.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Amir Khusrau lived earlier during the Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin Khilji, not in Akbar's court.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Vakil under the reign of Mughal Emperor Akbar, who received the title of Khan-i-Khanan?
questions.solution:
• Bairam Khan was the Vakil under Akbar and received the title of Khan-i-Khanan.
  • He was a prominent Mughal noble and military commander who served as Akbar's regent and chief minister during the early years of his reign.

questions.question: Which amongst the following statements is correct about Mughal emperor Akbar?
questions.option_1: He founded a new religion called 'Din-e-Ilahi'.
questions.option_2: He fought and won the third battle of Panipat against the Hindu King Hemu.
questions.option_4: He was highly educated and knew many languages.
questions.solution:
• Akbar founded a new religion called 'Din-e-Ilahi' (belief in one God).
  • The first initiated disciples included Birbal, Prince Salim (Jahangir), and Abul Fazl.
  • The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali, not involving Akbar.

questions.question: Who amongst the following Mughal emperors got classical Hindu mythological texts Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian?
questions.solution:
• Akbar got the Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian.
  • The Mahabharata was translated by Faizi and 'Abd al-Qadir Bada'uni and named Razmnamah.
  • Literature under Akbar: Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari written by Abu'l-Fazl.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Akbar are true?
1. He introduced the Mansabdari system.
2. He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire.
3. He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
questions.solution:
• Statements 1 and 3 are correct.
  • The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar in 1571 to rank government officials and military generals.
  • Akbar made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Bijapur was annexed by Aurangzeb in 1685, not Akbar.

questions.question: When Akbar introduced Mansabdari system, ______ was the lowest grade of Mansabdari.
questions.solution:
• The lowest grade of Mansabdari was ten (10).
  • Mansabdari was a grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary, and military responsibilities.
  • During Akbar's reign, the lowest rank was 10 and the highest was 10,000.

questions.question: When was Khandesh merged into the Mughal empire by Akbar?
questions.solution:
• Khandesh was merged into the Mughal empire by Akbar in 1601.
  • Khandesh was situated in the Tapti valley, Maharashtra, and was founded by Malik Raja Faruqi.
  • Major military campaigns by Akbar: Chittor (1568), Ranthambore (1569).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the defence of Chittorgarh Fort:
Statement 1: Jaimal and Patta were the Rajput warriors entrusted with defending the fort of Chittor against Akbar in 1567-1568.
Statement 2: The Siege of Chittorgarh was led by Sher Shah Suri against the Mewar kingdom.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Jaimal and Patta heroically defended Chittorgarh Fort during Akbar's siege of 1567-1568.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The siege was led by Akbar, not Sher Shah Suri.

questions.question: Tansen, the music legend, was a courtier in which of the following courts before coming to Akbar?
questions.solution:
• Tansen was initially the court singer of King Ram Chand of Rewa.
  • His original name was Ramtanu Pandey.
  • Tansen was the title given to him by Raja Vikramjit of Gwalior.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding land classification during Akbar's reign:
Statement 1: Chachar was the land that was always cultivated and never allowed to lie fallow.
Statement 2: Polaj was the ideal land that remained under continuous cultivation without being left fallow.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Chachar was land left fallow for three to four years, not continuously cultivated.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Polaj was the most fertile land that remained under constant cultivation without being left fallow.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was the first planned city of the Mughals?
questions.solution:
• Fatehpur Sikri was the first planned city of the Mughals.
  • It is located near Agra in Uttar Pradesh and was built by Akbar between 1571 and 1585.
  • Fatehpur Sikri was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

questions.question: When was the Battle of Tukaroi fought where Akbar defeated the Sultanate of Bengal and Bihar?
questions.solution:
• The Battle of Tukaroi (also known as the Battle of Bajhaura/Moghalmari) was fought in 1575 at Balasore (Odisha).
  • Akbar defeated Daud Khan Karrani (Ruler of Bengal).
  • The battle led to the Treaty of Katak, in which Daud Khan Karrani ceded Bengal and Bihar, retaining only Odisha.

questions.question: ______ administration became the model followed by the great emperor Akbar when he consolidated the Mughal Empire.
questions.solution:
• Sher Shah Suri's administration became the model followed by Akbar.
  • Although the Suri dynasty ruled for only 15 years, it introduced an efficient administration that borrowed elements from Alauddin Khilji.

questions.question: Ain-i Akbari, a document on life of Mughal ruler Akbar does not contain information about
questions.solution:
• Ain-i-Akbari does not contain information about Akbar's ancestors.
  • Abul Fazl wrote a three-volume history of Akbar's reign titled Akbarnama:
    • Volume 1: Akbar's ancestors
    • Volume 2: Events of Akbar's reign
    • Volume 3: Ain-i-Akbari
  • Ain-i-Akbari is divided into five volumes covering revenues, army, administration, etc.

questions.question: Ajmer became the suba headquarters under the
questions.solution:
• Ajmer became the suba headquarters under the Mughals.
  • Ajmer Subah was one of the original 12 subahs of the Mughal Empire (1526-1858), established during Akbar's administrative reforms of 1572-1580.

questions.question: In which year was Kashmir annexed to the Mughal Empire by Akbar?
questions.solution:
• Kashmir was annexed to the Mughal Empire by Akbar in 1586.
  • Other military conquests of Akbar: Malwa (1562), Gondwana (1564), Gujarat (1573), Mewar (1576), Bihar and Bengal (1576).

questions.question: As described in 'Ain-i Akbari' by Abul Fazl-i-Allami, 'gaz' (unit of measuring length) was divided into ______ equal parts called
questions.solution: • According to Ain-i-Akbari, 'gaz' (unit of measuring length) was divided into equal parts called 'tassuj'.

questions.question: Who among the following issued Mahzarnama in 1579?
questions.solution:
• Akbar issued Mahzarnama in 1579.
  • It was a declaration that gave authority to change the religious laws of Islam.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the foundation of Murshidabad:
Statement 1: The city of Makhsudabad, later known as Murshidabad, was built by Mughal emperor Akbar.
Statement 2: Murshidabad got its present name from Nawab Murshid Quli Khan.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is incorrect: Murshidabad was not built by Akbar; it developed later.
  • Statement 2 is correct: Murshidabad was renamed by Nawab Murshid Quli Khan in the early 18th century after his own name.

questions.question: In the context of Mughal administration, which of the following is the most appropriate definition of 'Abwab'?
questions.option_1: A clerk in the government treasury
questions.option_3: A tax levied on the lands over and above the original rent
questions.solution:
• 'Abwab' was a tax levied on lands over and above the original rent in Mughal India.
  • All temporary and circumstantial taxes and impositions levied by the government over and above regular taxes were called 'abwab'.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor is known for his extensive autobiography, Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri?
questions.solution:
• Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri (also known as Jahangirnama) is the autobiography of the fourth Mughal Emperor, Jahangir.
  • Written in Persian, it details the first nineteen years of his reign along with his personal reflections.
  • Akbar's reign is chronicled in Akbarnama by Abul Fazl; Shah Jahan's in Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Amar Singh of Mewar:
Statement 1: Amar Singh was the son of Rana Sanga and accepted Mughal service during the reign of Aurangzeb.
Statement 2: Amar Singh was the Sisodiya ruler of Mewar who surrendered to Akbar in 1600.
Which of the following is correct?
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
• Both statements are false.
  • Amar Singh was the son of Maharana Pratap, not Rana Sanga.
  • He submitted to Jahangir in 1615, not to Akbar or Aurangzeb.

questions.question: Who succeeded in securing trading concessions for the East India Company from Mughal Emperor Jahangir?
questions.solution:
• Sir Thomas Roe succeeded in securing trading concessions for the East India Company from Jahangir in 1615.
  • John Mildenhall was the first British explorer to make an overland journey to India.
  • Captain William Hawkins visited Jahangir's court in 1608.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the biography of Jahangir known as Iqbalnama-i-Jahangiri?
questions.solution:
• Mutamid Khan wrote Iqbalnama-i-Jahangiri.
  • He was in the court of Mughal Emperor Jahangir (4th Mughal ruler, 1605-1627).
  • The book was written in Persian and covers the first 19 years of Jahangir's reign.

questions.question: Sarai Nurmahal is a centrally protected monument of India. It is situated in which state of India?
questions.solution:
• Sarai Nurmahal is situated in Punjab (Jalandhar).
  • Shalimar Bagh, Begum Shahi Mosque, and Bachcha Taj are monuments built by Jahangir.
